findings.title: Gate-value serialization quirk in run_scored.py pass-list filter (latent, conservative, non-outcome-affecting here)
findings.detail: In the committed ledger, G1/G2/G5 serialize as strings ("True"/"False") while G3/G4/G6/G7 serialize as JSON booleans — numpy boolean lineage hit json default=str. The candidates_passing_G1_G7 filter checks `v in (True, "PASS", ...)` which does NOT match the string "True": had a candidate substantively passed all gates, the pass list would still have shown empty (a false NEGATIVE, never a false positive). In THIS run the outcome is unaffected and double-verified: the auditor's own pure-Python arithmetic confirms all 4 candidates fail G1-G7 substantively (G3 and/or G5 fail in every arm; G6 kills two; one arm fails G1/G2; one fails G4). Terminal verdict does not depend on the pass list.
